text.text_excerpt: I've been trying to eat a bit healthier lately, but I allow myself the weekend to splurge on the good stuff, so I ended up at Lakeview Harbor for a cheeseburger and onion rings. Truth me told: I never went to the old Lakeview Harbor. I had always heard raves about how good the burgers are, but I rarely eat burgers these days, and when I do, I go for Company Burger. This new spot is really nice and the inside is set up nicely and is quite welcoming. I was here right when they opened, so the crowd was thin and I was seated immediately. As I mentioned, I got the cheeseburger with onion rings and also a side of potato salad because...salad is healthy. Duh. The cheeseburger comes cooked any wa...

Before the burger craze took over New Orleans, there were only a few dedicated burger joints in the city; and the big three back in the day (in my opinion) were Port of Call, Snug Harbor and Ground Pati. Shortly after I graduated college way back when in 1993 (yeah I know I'm old), Lakeview Harbor opened its doors and I have been a fan ever since. This place is all about the burgers. They start with a freshly ground, hand formed USDA beef burger and grill it any way you want. I like my burgers medium rare and many restaurants will only cook their burgers medium or well done. Lakeview Harbor is a burger lover's paradise. I went here recently with a large party after not having been for a while. It was good to see that not much had changed. The place is still decorated in a nautical theme. It also still has a jukebox that is far too loud especially if some customer decides to play some inappropriate dining music. Lastly, it still has very good burgers. On this trip I went with the plain ole hamburger cooked medium. Low and behold it actually came out medium. It was a large hand formed patty which was juicy and flavorful. For a side I had the loaded baked potato which was perfectly cooked and loaded in every sense of the word.
